sentences.text: This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 11.04.2022 at about 7.00 p.m. he was walking on left side of the road near Nandini Milk Booth, Andrahalli Main Road, Vidyamanynagara, Bengaluru,
at SCCH-5

that time, a car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-8976 came from back side at very high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Athishaya Hospital,
Andrahalli, after firstaid he was shifted to K.C.General Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for 15 days and towards conveyance, food and nourishment, he has spent an amount of Rs.50,000/-.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 39 years, hale and healthy, working as helper at private factory, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is still suffering from pain,
he is under deep mental agony, he cannot do his work as he was doing earlier.
Out of this accident crime No.186/2022 is registered against the driver of the said car before the SCCH-5 Byadarahalli Police.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further submitted that, there is 14 days delay in lodging the police complaint, hence respondent No.2 has denied involvement of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-8976 in the alleged accident.

Further submitted that, as per MLC Extract of K.C.General Hospital, history of RTA is mentioned as 'fall from bike last night', so that, there is no involvement of the offending car in the alleged SCCH-5 accident.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further denied issuance of insurance policy to the said car and if there is any issuance of policy, it is subject to confirmation from the concerned branch.
Further the driver of the offending car did not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
Mohana.G vs Vinod.P on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164159865/
2

1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.04.2022 at about 7.00 p.m. when petitioner reached near Nandini Milk Booth, Andrahalli Main Road, Vidyamanyanagara,
Bengaluru at that time, one Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C- SCCH-5 8976 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2 and marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his evidence.

On the other hand, Senior Medical Officer, K.C.General Hospital is examined as RW-1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.D.1 and Ex.D.2, Deputy Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-2 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.3 and Ex.R.4 and closed his evidence.
SCCH-5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.5,
SCCH-5 copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
Sec.133 notice, reply, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 11.04.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

On the other hand, Senior Medical Officer of K.C.General Hospital is examined as RW-1 and copy of consultant/specialist note and orders is marked as Ex.D.1, copy of discharge summary is Mohana.G vs Vinod.P on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164159865/
3 marked as Ex.D.2.
Further Deputy Manager of respondent No.2 Insurance Company is examined as RW-2 and exhibited SCCH-5 authorization letter marked as Ex.R.3 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.4.
Further except oral evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 11.04.2022 at about 7.00 p.m. when he was walking on left side of the road near Nandini Milk Booth, Andrahalli Main Road,
Vidyamanyanagara, Bengaluru.

11. Ofcourse as per respondent No.2 written arguments, in Ex.D.2 issued by K.C.General Hospital stated that, fall from bike last night by the petitioner alone is not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because there is no other corroborative materials on SCCH-5 respondent side to believe Ex.D.2.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-8976.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left ankle bimalleolar fracture.
In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7 issued by K.C.General SCCH-5 Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 12.04.2022 to 25.04.2022.
14. Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited clinical examination is marked as Ex.P.10 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.11 and he has assessed physical disability of the left lower limbs at 36% and whole body physical disability of 12%.
In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner.
Further deposed that, fracture is united and implants are insitu.
Further deposed that, petitioner can walk without any aid and ca do desk job.

Under such circumstances,
considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the SCCH-5 petitioner is considered at the rate of 12% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 36% of lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 39 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 1983 and accident was occurred in the year 2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.10 his age is considered about 39 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

4 16.
As per his case, he was working as helper at private factory, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
SCCH-5

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7 issued by K.C.General Hospital, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 12.04.2022 to 25.04.2022 i.e., for 13 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the SCCH-5 guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,750/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,392/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18. Further petitioner has not produced any medical bills towards the expenses incurred by him for treatment and also he has not produced discharge summary towards the treatment taken by him.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.Sanjeev Kumar D.L. has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on11.04.2022.
So as per Ex.P.7 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained bimalleolar fracture SCCH-5 of let ankle, for which he underwent surgery of ORIF with screws and plating.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Vinod P. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
19.
Per contra, except oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondent No.2 has filed written statement, cross-examined and filed written arguments and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case,
because it is bounden duty of them to prove the SCCH-5 defence as taken in the written statement.

Ofcourse in the written arguments of respondent No.2, he has reiterated the entire avemrents of the written statement and evidence of RW-2 and Ex.D.2, but they have not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case.
20. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl. No

. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
Mohana.G vs Vinod.P on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164159865/
5 1. Loss of Future Income 3,18,600-00 2. Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 5. Loss of income during laid up 6,392-00 period

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,69,992/- with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.991792123380007455 which is valid for the period from 12.11.2021 to 11.11.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.04.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Hence respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

SCCH-5 The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,69,992/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Sixty Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Two Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 7th day of January, 2025)
